## Props (4)

| Prop | Type | Required | Declared default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `as` | `VisuallyHiddenElement \| undefined` | no | `"span"` | HTML element to render. Defaults to 'span'. |
| `focusable` | `boolean \| undefined` | no | `false` | When true, the content becomes visible when it (or a focusable descendant) receives keyboard focus — the skip-link pattern. Defaults to false. |
| `id` | `string \| undefined` | no | — | Accessible identifier (e.g. for `aria-labelledby`/`aria-describedby` references). |
| `ui` | `Partial<Record<"root", DzClassValue>> \| undefined` | no | `undefined` | Per-part class overrides, keyed by the names in `DzVisuallyHidden.anatomy.ts` (ADR-19 §5). `class` keeps its existing meaning and its existing target; `ui` addresses the other parts by name, and a typo is a type error. |

## Usage (from `packages/core/stories/typography/DzVisuallyHidden.stories.ts`, story `Default`)

```vue

      <div class="space-y-3 max-w-md">
        <p class="text-sm text-[var(--dz-muted-foreground)]">
          Press <kbd class="px-1 border border-[var(--dz-border)] rounded">Tab</kbd> to focus the
          element below. With <code>focusable</code> on it reveals itself in place; switch it off,
          or change <code>as</code> to a non-focusable element such as <code>span</code>, and it
          stays in the accessibility tree only — inspect it with the a11y panel.
        </p>
        <DzVisuallyHidden
          v-bind="args"
          href="#main"
          class="bg-[var(--dz-primary)] text-[var(--dz-primary-foreground)] px-3 py-2 rounded"
        >
          Skip to main content
        </DzVisuallyHidden>
        <div id="main" class="border border-[var(--dz-border)] rounded p-4 text-sm">Main content region.</div>
      </div>
    
```

## Parts, states and tokens

**Parts** — addressable nodes, emitted as `data-part`. Reach one with the selector, or pass
classes by name through the typed `ui` prop; a typo in `ui` is a type error rather than a class
that lands nowhere.

When your `class` and a `ui` entry set the same Tailwind utility, **your `class` wins**: the
merge order is recipe → `ui` → `class`, and `cn()` is tailwind-merge, so the last one through
takes effect. That is what lets you restyle a wrapper someone else built without `!important`.

| Part | Selector | Always present |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `root` | `[data-part="root"]` | yes |

```vue
<DzVisuallyHidden :ui="{ 'root': 'ring-2' }" />
```

**States** — the values `data-state` may take, plus the presence-only boolean attributes.

This component declares no states: nothing about it is advertised to CSS or to a test.

**Component tokens** — the custom properties this component reads, and therefore every one you
may set. The list is the complete supported override surface; any other `--dz-*` it inherits is
not a promise.

This component declares no component tokens of its own: it is styled entirely from the global
semantic layer, which the theme owns.
